Endorsements
Joanna Solmonsohn, New York State Nurses Association
"This endorsement acknowledges your
commitment to not only supporting our members but also addressing the issues affecting
healthcare access and the
needs of working New Yorkers." -Joanna Solmonsohn
Communications Workers of America

CWA is a labor union where working people join together to strengthen their voice in their jobs and communities. Members work not just in the communications and information industries, but also in the news media, the airlines, broadcast and cable television, public service, higher education and health care, manufacturing, in high tech and more.
Abigail Martin,
Executive Director of Eleanor’s Legacy
"This endorsement reflects our
confidence in your leadership, your
commitment to advancing Democratic values, and your dedication to
protecting and
expanding reproductive rights across New York State. We are proud to stand with you and to support the important work you are undertaking in your community." -Abigail Martin
New York League of Conservation Voters

NYLCV is the only statewide environmental organization in New York that fights for clean water, clean air, renewable energy and open space through political action. NYLCV is non-partisan, pragmatic and effective.
Moms Demand Action

Moms Demand Action is a grassroots movement of Americans fighting for public safety measures that can protect people from gun violence. We pass stronger gun laws and work to close the loopholes that jeopardize the safety of our families. We also work in our own communities and with business leaders to encourage a culture of responsible gun ownership. We know that gun violence is preventable, and we’re committed to doing what it takes to keep families safe.
Mary E. Sullivan, President of CSEA

"From State agencies and local government to schools, healthcare facilities, home-based child care providers, and the private sector, CSEA members provide the services that New Yorkers rely on every day. As New York continues to focus on recruiting and retaining a strong workforce, we need elected officials like you who will fight to make public service more accessible, respected, and rewarding."
Mary E. Sullivan
Suffolk County Superior Officers Association

The Suffolk County Superior Association represents over 1,000 Active and Retired Supervisors in the Suffolk County Police Department. Their mission is to promote and develop a friendly spirit and preserve morale among membership.
3.14 Action Fund

3.14 Action is the only organization in the United States focused on recruiting, training, and electing Democrats with a background in science to public office. 3.14 Action is dedicated to electing candidates who will ensure fact-driven legislation when elected.
32BJ SEIU

32BJ is 185,000 working men and women just like you joined together for dignity and respect on the job. Together, we fight for and win the higher wages, quality healthcare, protections at work and other benefits you need for your family and community to thrive.
1199 SEIU

1199SEIU caregivers are proud to endorse these candidates who will fight for frontline healthcare workers, our patients, and our communities.” As New Yorkers confront unprecedented attacks from the federal government, we need real leaders who will stand up for good union jobs, quality healthcare, affordable housing, and civil rights. From Long Island to Buffalo, 1199SEIU healthcare workers are ready to volunteer knocking doors, talking to voters, and doing whatever it takes to ensure that working people win this November.
Act Jew

Act Jew is a civic engagement organization that mobilizes Jewish communities to participate meaningfully in democratic life. Act Jew increases Jewish visibility through education while protecting the safety and dignity of Jewish life.
W.J Fleischmann, Chairman of NYSLB

As Assemblywomen, you continue to demonstrate your commitment to Labor and the working families of New York State. Your unwavering advocacy for the safety and rights of workers has earned you the full backing of our Organization.
Communication Workers of America Local 1109

Communication Workers of America is a labor union that represents workers in the telecommunications, technology, airline, healthcare, and service industries. The CWA is the largest communications and media labor union in the United States, representing over 700,000 American workers.
John Feinblatt, President of Everytown for Gun Safety
The American people want leaders who will put public safety ahead of gun industry profits, and these candidates will bring that fight to every level of government
LIUNA-NY

LIUNA-NY is a partnership of the New York State Laborers’ PAC, Mason Tenders’ District Council PAC, Greater New York LECET, New York State LECET and New York State Health and Safety Fund. LIUNA-NY focuses on advancing the industry through aggressive organizing, legislative advocacy and robust education campaigns.
Anthony Villa, Regional Manager for Eastern New York

Our Council represents over 28,000 members who are dedicated to their craft and who set the highest standards for skills in the construction industry. We believe in developing and maintaining intelligent labor laws that can serve honest workers and honest employees.
NYSUT

New York State United Teachers represents over 140,000 New York teachers, college employees, and healthcare workers. NYSUT is dedicated to not only improving working conditions but also the profession itself. NYSUT is a grassroots organization, and its mission is to elect representatives who will proactively lead.
Robin Chappelle Golston, Chair of PPESV, and Vincent Russell, Endorsement Committee

New York State has long been a leader in championing reproductive health access. At a time when our health, rights, and freedoms are being relentlessly attacked - now more than ever, we need state leaders who will advance bold policies and actions to further New York State’s legacy as a leader in protecting and expanding access to care. We believe you will be one of those leaders.
Suffolk County Association of Municipal Employees

Suffolk AME (Association of Municipal Employees) is the largest independent Union in Suffolk County. Representing more than 6,000 active and retired public employees, AME negotiates and enforces equitable contracts for its membership and helps ensure a skilled, dedicated, and educated workforce for Suffolk County. Made up of 30 different Unit Boards ranging from Consumer Affairs and Civil Service, Crossing Guards, DPW, and Fire, Rescue and Emergency Services, to Vector Control, Suffolk County Community College, the Department of Social Services, and more, our members perform the literally hundreds of jobs needed to keep Suffolk County operational on a day-to-day basis, and our Union works to advocate on their behalf every single day.
Suffolk County Correction Officers Association Coalition
The Suffolk County Correction Officers Association represents over 850 of Suffolk’s boldest men and women working in our correctional facilities throughout Suffolk County, NY.
Suffolk County Deputy Sheriff PBA Coalition
Our primary mission is to provide quality representation for Suffolk County Deputy Sheriffs as well as promote a positive relationship with our community.
Suffolk County Detective Investigators PBA Coalition

The Suffolk County Detective Investigator’s PBA represents the sworn Investigators of the Suffolk County District Attorney’s office. The DIPBA seeks to protect and advance the rights and interests of the membership while fostering camaraderie and fellowship with other police organizations.
Louis Civello, President of Suffolk County PBA

The Police Benevolent Association reconizes and appreciates your unwavering support of law enforcement officers, who continue to risk their lives to keep our communities safe. Your leadership and commitment to public safety have earned our full support.
Suffolk County Police Conference Coalition

The Suffolk County Police Conference is an organization of Professional Law Enforcement Officers from the State, County, Town, and Village Police Departments operating within the County of Suffolk, New York. The Conference was organized in 1947 and incorporated in 1950. Our Motto is “Proud of our Police.”
Suffolk County Police Department Detective Association Coalition
The Suffolk County Police Department Detective Association Coalition is the union arm of the Suffolk County Police Department Detectives.
Suffolk County Probation Coalition

The Suffolk County Probation Officers Association was incorporated as a fraternal organization on July 22, 1983. Our members are dedicated to serving the citizens of Suffolk County with the highest degree of professionalism. The Suffolk County Probation Officer’s Association is proud to represent each of our hard-working and devoted members.
Albert Fredricks, Political Chair of the Sierra Club Long Island Group

Our endorsement is based on your demonstrated commitment to environmental protection and our expectation that, going forward, you will continue to work diligently to preserve and enhance Long Island’s precious environmental resources.
They See Blue New York

The They See Blue organization seeks to create a civil connection among like-minded South Asian to advance civic engagement across the country. They See Blue’s mission is to mobilize and engage Americans of Southeast Asian descent in the Democratic process.
Allie Taylor, Board of Directors of Voters for Animal Rights
We appreciate your understanding of animal issues and your history of supporting animal legislation. We are excited to support leaders who share our vision for a more compassionate New York.
New York State AFL-CIO

The New York State AFL-CIO is a federation of 3,000 affiliated public sector, private sector, and building trades unions throughout the state, representing 2.5 million members, retirees and their families. Our members live and work in every community in our state, and reflect the diversity that makes New York great.
Long Island Federation of Labor AFL-CIO

The 250,000 member Long Island Federation of Labor, AFL-CIO, represents a wide range of union workers from teachers to technicians, public employees to painters, bus drivers to bricklayers, retail, auto, janitorial, utility, health care and construction workers. The Federation is the voice for the Long Island labor movement. It speaks on behalf of Long Island’s working families and its affiliated local unions to political leaders and legislative bodies at every level of government
Michael O'Meara, President
of the Police Conference of New York

The PCNY, formed in 1925, is a statewide labor union today comprising hundreds of police unions and groups representing more than 50,000 professional police officers, and is the largest police organization in the state. Our representation stretches across the entire state, from the tip of Montauk Point to the Canadian border. PCNY membership is comprised of local, county, city, and state police, along with groups as diverse as the MTA Police and the Port Authority Police.
The New York State Public Employees Federation

The New York State Public Employees Federation (PEF) is a union that represents approximately 55,000 state employees with professional, scientific, and technical titles. Our members work in more than 3,000 different titles in every state agency, including nurses, social workers, doctors, engineers, counselors, parole officers, lawyers, IT specialists, teachers, habilitation specialists, therapists, and many more.
National Organization for women Mid-suffolk NY0506

As the grassroots arm of the women’s movement, the National Organization for Women is dedicated to its multi-issue and multi-strategy approach to women’s rights, and is the largest organization of feminist grassroots activists in the United States. NOW chapters focus on six priority issues including reproductive rights, ending sex discrimination/constitutional equality, promoting diversity and ending racism, economic justice, stopping violence against women, and LGBTQIA rights.
Streets PAC

StreetsPAC is dedicated to electing public officials who are committed to improving the safety, mobility, and livability of one of New York City’s greatest assets: our streets. Our sidewalks, roads, and plazas account for the majority of all public space in New York City and are a precious resource to be used and enjoyed by all. StreetsPAC supports candidates for public office who will champion Safe, Complete and Livable Streets.
Italian American Political Action Committee

We are a non-partisan organization committed to empowering the Italian-American community through civic engagement, advocacy, and leadership development. Our mission is to ensure our community is represented and actively involved in shaping the future.​ Through collaboration and dedication, we connect individuals with opportunities that create real impact and lasting change.
Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers Local Union #1

Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers Local 1, NY is dedicated to the craft of bricklaying, stonesetting, stone tending, masonry restoration and plastering. With over 5000 of the most talented masonry craft workers hailing not just from the New York City and Long Island area but from around the world, these Union members are responsible for some of the “who’s who" of buildings, including Grand Central Terminal, Yankee Stadium, Citifield, the World Trade Center Memorial, the Chrysler Building, the Met-Life Building, the American Museum of Natural History, Lincoln Center, the Cloisters, the Frick, the Metropolitan Museum, as well as thousands of office and residential buildings.
Bricklayers and Allied Craftworkers Local Union #7

Local 7 is a Mega Local formed by merging several individual BAC Allied Crafts into one autonomous unit. The leadership and members of the BAC have always supported the middle class by helping to establish the 8-hour work day, 5-day work week, implementing health insurance and pensions for it’s members, negotiating higher wages, teaching safety and related training, supporting the family and medical leave act and encouraging fair treatment for women, people of all ethnic backgrounds, and those with disabilities.
The Long Island Rail Road Bargaining Coalition

Both your support during our contract fight and your record on other issues before the New York State Assembly show that you are a champion and fighter for workers and their families, including our members who keep the Long Island Rail Road moving every day. Because you went above and beyond for us during our contract fight and because of your record fighting for our members and their livelihoods and working-class people in general, we are proud to offer you our endorsement for your re-election to New York’s 4th Assembly District.
Newsday Opinion

Rebecca A. Kassay is completing her first term in the Assembly, but the Port Jefferson Democrat already has made her mark. For the last two years, Kassay, 37, didn’t give up on the notion of transferring part of the former Lawrence Aviation Industries property to the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, paving the way for a future rail yard, a new Long Island Rail Road station and, perhaps, the electrification of the Port Jefferson Branch. It wasn’t easy. But Kassay kept writing and rewriting legislation, meeting with stakeholders, and using her bully pulpit until the deal finally closed last month, opening doors for future transit improvements and preserving the important Setauket-Port Jefferson Station Greenway.
Coram Civic Association

The Board of Directors for The Coram Civic Association is a testament to the power of volunteerism and civic engagement. Comprised of dedicated residents from all walks of life, these unpaid members unite under a common vision: to foster a future where safety and security are accessible to every inhabitant of Coram. The board works tirelessly without any financial compensation, driven by a deep love for their community and an unwavering belief in the transformative power of collective action. Through their efforts, they embody the spirit of service and community leadership, working to turn their shared aspirations into tangible realities for the benefit of all.
Brian McDonnell, Political and Legislative Director

AFSCME members value elected officials who will stand with them and make their voices heard in Albany. AFSCME represents workers in every city, county, town, village, and school district in New York State, as well as people who care for the sick and the elderly in public hospitals and nursing homes. Our members deliver services to those with disabilities, the infirm, and the most vulnerable in our state. Our law enforcement members maintain public safety and security. The AFSCME membership keeps our state running every day. New York works because our members do.
Michael Florio, Chief Executive Office of LIBI & Grant Havasy, Chairman of LIBI PAC

On behalf of the Long Island Builders Institute Political Action Committee, we are pleased to recognize you as a “Smart Growth Housing Candidate” for the 2026 election. This designation reflects your understanding of the needs and challenges facing Long Island's homebuilding and remodeling industry, as well as the importance of responsible growth and expanding housing opportunities across our region.
Messenger Papers

The Port Jefferson Democrat, we think, is carefully navigating the brutal politics of the Albany majority, while also balancing local needs. Some big wins for her came in the form of State aid for the Mill Pond Dam, helping secure the Lawrence Aviation site in Port Jefferson Station for eventual rail electrification, and getting a bill through to increase accountability on the mobile gaming epidemic.
Times Beacon Record News Media

Rebecca Kassay has demonstrated an understanding of the district’s needs through her work on environmental protection, public safety, affordability, and local infrastructure. Her first term has also shown the value of having a representative who understands the community beyond the walls of the Capitol.
Chris Rola, PBA of New York State President

The PBA of New York State is proud to announce our endorsement of these candidates for the New York State Legislature in 2026. We are confident they possess the leadership, integrity, and commitment necessary to effectively serve the residents of New York. Our members proudly serve and protect communities, campuses, parks, waterways, forests, and public lands across New York State. We recognize leaders who prioritize public safety, support labor and law enforcement, and understand the essential role first responders play. Strong partnerships with state leaders are essential to advancing policies and protections that support our officers and the communities they serve. The PBA of New York State is confident these endorsed candidates will serve with professionalism, accountability, and dedication.
